label: prf:hecke-satisfies-blitvic-hypothesis
title: Proof: Hecke generators satisfy Blitvić's pair-partition hypothesis
html:
Proof. We reduce an arbitrary joint moment of centred generators to a pair-partition sum by induction on word length.

Setup. Let \tilde\sigma_i := \sigma_i - z \cdot 1 where z = q^3/(q^2+1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) (convention D; under the excised convention C the shift \sigma_i - z\cdot 1 was not centred at all, leaving \mathrm{tr}_M(\tilde\sigma_i) = 0.1134 rather than 0), so that \mathrm{tr}_M(\tilde\sigma_i) = 0. The argument uses only joint \mathrm{tr}_M-moments of the \tilde\sigma_i; no adjoint structure is required. (Note that \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i^{-1}) = z - (q - q^{-1}) \neq z (Markov axioms), so \tilde\sigma_i is not fixed by the bar-involution \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}; Blitvić's hypothesis is a moment condition and does not need it.)

Odd length vanishes. For k odd, every reduction of \tilde\sigma_{i_1} \tilde\sigma_{i_2} \cdots \tilde\sigma_{i_k} via the Hecke relation leaves at least one unmatched single \tilde\sigma_i factor; by Markov property applied at that factor, \mathrm{tr}_M(x \cdot \tilde\sigma_i) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x \cdot \sigma_i) - z \mathrm{tr}_M(x) = z \mathrm{tr}_M(x) - z \mathrm{tr}_M(x) = 0. The entire word vanishes under \mathrm{tr}_M.

Even length reduces to pair-partitions. For k even, proceed by induction on the number of generator types appearing. The base case k = 2 is the variance computation:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\tilde\sigma_i \tilde\sigma_j)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i \sigma_j) - z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) -
  z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_j) + z^2.

For i \neq j with |i - j| \geq 2, far-commutativity gives \sigma_i \sigma_j = \sigma_j \sigma_i and the trace property yields \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i \sigma_j) = z^2; the centred moment is z^2 - z^2 - z^2 + z^2 = 0.

For i = j, apply the Hecke quadratic relation: \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1}) \sigma_i + 1, so \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i^2) = (q - q^{-1}) z + 1. The centred moment is

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\tilde\sigma_i^2)
  \;=\;
  (q - q^{-1}) z + 1 - 2 z^2 + z^2
  \;=\;
  (q - q^{-1}) z + 1 - z^2,

which is positive in the Wenzl regime q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2} > 2 (centred Hecke variance positivity).

The general matching is therefore \mathrm{tr}_M(\tilde\sigma_i \tilde\sigma_j) = \bigl[(q - q^{-1}) z + 1 - z^2\bigr] \cdot \delta_{i = j}, which is the case k = 2 of the pair-partition formula.

Inductive step. For general k, apply the Hecke quadratic relation iteratively to reduce any repeated generator \sigma_i^2 to a lower-degree word. This produces a tree of reductions whose leaves are square-free generator products; each leaf evaluates under \mathrm{tr}_M via Wenzl's product factorisation (prop:trace-locality-meets-gs-non-locality). The factorisation pairs each \tilde\sigma_i with another \tilde\sigma_j of the same index (Kronecker \delta_{i=j}) — any unmatched generator gives zero by Markov property as above.

The induction shows the joint moment is a sum, indexed by pair-partitions \pi of \{1, \ldots, k\}, of products of length-2 moments times a crossing-count weight from the braid relations. Explicitly:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\tilde\sigma_{i_1} \cdots \tilde\sigma_{i_k}\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\pi \in P_2(k)}
    q^{\mathrm{cr}(\pi)} \cdot
    \prod_{\{a, b\} \in \pi}
      \bigl((q - q^{-1}) z + 1 - z^2\bigr) \cdot
      \delta_{i_a = i_b},

where \mathrm{cr}(\pi) is the number of crossings of \pi. This matches Blitvić's (q, t)-Gaussian moment formula [blitvic2012, eq. (1.2)] at parameter (q, t = 1). \square
